speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have right leg weakness, an unsteady gait, multiple falls, forgetfulness, and paranoid behavior. To understand the progression and location of your symptoms, can you tell me exactly when these issues first started and if they have been getting worse over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Posterior Cerebral Artery (PCA) Infarction with Wernicke's Encephalopathy or Frontotemporal Dementia with vascular involvement. The acute 1-week onset of focal motor weakness and ataxia combined with a 6-month prodrome of memory loss and behavioral changes (paranoia, agitation) suggests a subacute stroke or a rapidly progressive neurodegenerative process affecting the right posterior circulation and frontal/temporal lobes. I need to confirm if the gait disturbance is purely ataxic or if there is associated nystagmus and confusion, which would point towards Wernicke's encephalopathy. Can you tell me if the patient experiences any double vision, difficulty swallowing, or if there is a history of heavy alcohol use? REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with Diffusion Weighted Imaging.
